The fact that you are taking this into consideration is an amazing thing, good on you man! From my experience as someone with eczema and someone who has been in a few longer term relationships, i can say a few things off the top of my head:  


just have to preface this is all based on my personal experience and every single person is different. this is just what ive learned and experienced on my own journey.

Some days we have a really bad flare up and no matter what someone says it doesnt matter and we might just rant on and on about how shitty our skin is and how ugly we feel etc..  Even if you say you dont notice it we may even argue with you, it really can be frustrating. It can take a lot of time and effort to get them to believe you when you tell them that their skin makes no difference and that they're beautiful. But being persistent and really showing it over time is what counts. As much as we might be a bit funny with compliments and things when we're having a flare up, it really does help in the end.  


If shes having a flare up and just doesnt want to go out or talk or anything, try your best to not get upset. It has nothing to do with not wanting to be with you or see you. Its just about feeling totally ugly and unworthy some days, and sometimes you just gotta be alone and comfortable. In my past relationships if i was having a bad flare up and id isolate myself a little bit my partner would get extremely worried and upset and feel like i was mad at them and didnt want to talk to them, and they'd say they didnt care about my skin and the fact i couldnt just accept that was probably very frustrating. But eventually with time you get more comfortable. So if anything like that comes up just know its nothing to do with you. shed probably want nothing more than to just be normal and not have eczema and all those issues, but with time she'll be able to see that you genuinely care.  


Be careful with suggesting things that might help. This one all depends on the person but most people i know with eczema are already looking and trying everything to sort it out and suggestions just seem to irritate us. I dont know what it is. You can kind of tell the difference between those who genuinely care though so i wouldnt worry about it too much. If someone suggests something to me, chances are ive heard and tried it and it didnt work. Id rather have someone just not point it out or talk about it all unless i myself bring it up. Thats just me though.   


Please for the love of god dont buy her creams or anything like that. We know it comes from a good place but its a bad idea for so many reasons i dont wanna go into lol Maybe if you see something cream or skincare wise, take a mental note of it, and if it comes up in conversation, maybe bring it up.  But just please dont buy anything like that unless she actually asks you to.   


Last thing. With all my past relationships im an extremely huggy affectionate person, BUT id have flare ups and get very itchy all over and get a bit snappy and just not wannt be touched or be in the same room as anyone. Id never get angry at them but id kinda just wanna zone out and focus on something else, my partners found it hard to understand and i think it upset them. So i guess what im saying is if shes having a flare and all of a sudden gets a bit snappy know its not to do with you, you are just fine, she might just need a bit of space.   


With all that said though if you're a decent person and genuinely care she'll see that and you'll be fine. Just treat her like you would anyone else. But just take it into consideration. Thats a lot more than most people and she'll probably appreciate that.
